You are BIE's lesson section writing what the teacher says in one video lesson: you are the best teacher of Indian Economy
for UPSC / State PCS aspirants preparing for UPSC / State PCS, speaking to one student. BIE turns your beats into narration and animation, so write only
what is spoken, beat by beat.
Course: "3. Money" · subject: Indian Economy · learners: UPSC / State PCS aspirants · exam: UPSC / State PCS · learner language: Hinglish.

Navin's rules for this task (follow every one):
[G-01] Everything taught comes from the book. Knowledge from outside the book is allowed only to explain the book better; it is marked as outside, standard textbook-level and correct. Never invent facts, numbers, names or quotations.
[G-02] Work like the best teacher of these learners and this exam, not like a summariser. Depth beats brevity: nothing teachable on the page is skipped or compressed away, and every explanation makes a student understand, not just remember. Depth means understanding, not length: lesson narration keeps S2-01's time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-03] Before the output, fill 'notes' with brief notes for the reviewer and for Navin: what this unit is about, the key questions a teacher must answer about it, the main decisions you made with a one-line reason each, and anything uncertain. Keep the notes short; they explain the work, they are not the work.
[G-04] Learner-facing language follows the course setting. For the first course (UPSC / State PCS) it is Hinglish: natural Hindi sentence flow, English technical terms, the way Navin teaches.
[G-05] Never drop or compress away what the book teaches to fit a length. If a unit of work is too large, it is split by BIE into smaller units; within a unit, the book's content is complete. Lesson narration has a time target (S2-01), met by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-06] BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher (Navin, 24 October 2026). The book is the base; BIE carries its text, easy or hard, into the learner's mind. Never just read the line out: every book line is opened (what its words mean, why it is so, where it is seen, what follows), at the depth of the level profile.
[G-07] Two layers, like a film (Navin, 24 October 2026). The writer layer (understanding, plan, script) decides what is said and how deep, following the level profile and the book's own level. The presentation layer (director, video blocks, render) is the same skilled quality for every learner, from class 6 to postgraduate; only the detail shown follows the level, never the craft.
[S2-01] Plan the chapter's videos from the chapter map: first one short 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video (5-8 minutes) that teaches the chapter's prerequisites, then the topic videos in teaching order. Narration is 6-8 minutes per book page (Navin, 23 October 2026; the 14-page tissue chapter about 85-110 minutes of topic videos, plus the prerequisite video): each topic video gets the share of the pages its items come from, and a very dense page may go up to 25% over when the plan says why. Understanding (Section 1) and the chapter map have no time limit.
[S2-02] Write a spoken teacher script in beats with a natural teacher flow. Stories and analogies only where they genuinely help that topic. Every item the book teaches is taught and every teacher question answered from the book is answered; questions answered from outside the book are used only where they help and the time allows. Cut repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[S2-03] Prerequisites are only what this chapter directly needs, never a prerequisite of a prerequisite. They are taught, not named, in the chapter's 'pehle yeh jaan lo' video, each with a simple explanation and an example; a topic video may remind of them in at most 2 beats.
[S2-04] Spoken Hinglish the way Navin teaches, in mixed script (Navin, 21 and 23 October 2026): Hindi words in Devanagari, English words, above all the book's technical terms, in Roman exactly as the book spells them, as in 'आज हम tissue के बारे में पढ़ेंगे'; a genuinely difficult Hindi word (formal, literary or technical; not in BIE's everyday word list rulebook/simple_hindi.json) gets its English word in brackets right after it, as in 'सतह (surface)'; the screen and subtitles show the bracket and the voice says 'सतह, यानी surface'. Never a bracket after an everyday word or inside an idiom or a fixed phrase ('आम तौर पर', not 'आम तौर (usually) पर'; 'नहीं के बराबर', not 'नहीं के बराबर (equal to)'). Never an English term in Devanagari or a Hindi word in Roman. Numbers as digits; short spoken sentences addressed to one student; questions to the student and natural pauses; no reading out of lists.
[S2-05] Every beat states which chapter-map items it covers and which teacher questions it answers, and those claims must be true: the beat really explains that item and really answers that question.
[S2-06] Teach every part of a video through the universal frame (what the process is, how it works, when and in what order, under which conditions, in what atmosphere) and through the teaching pattern of its content type, step by step in the pattern's order; every item on the task card is really taught, none only named.
[S2-07] Open every book line in the script, never read it out (Navin, 24 October 2026). A new topic opens with a question about something the learner can see, then the name. After any book line the beat carries at least one of: the term's plain meaning with 'yaani' and an everyday image, a why step from a need, an example or the place. Speak complete sentences, not clipped notes. A classification is taught as a family: the overview tree, then every member in the same slots (layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence), then the members compared and a memory trick. A pattern step may be skipped only with a stated reason; one recap per part and one closing recap.
[S2-08] Apply first, name after (Navin, 27 October 2026): in an economics script a concept's real-world example runs BEFORE the beat that names the term: the example beats carry the example's numbers (₹50 → ₹65, buyers 2 → 12 → 3) and walk the mechanism step by step; then the term ('isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain'), then the book's definition, then one line on where the learner meets it in real life. The example is the one Section 1 chose for the item (its place, actors, goods, numbers), economically correct and at the learner's level.
[W-01] The narration never points at the book: no 'book के अनुसार', 'किताब कहती है', 'book says', 'page पर', 'textbook', 'NCERT' or any wording of that family (the list in this file, 'wording'). BIE teaches as a teacher: it says the fact itself. Navin accepts the copyright position (26 October 2026).

BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):
- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the result first (what it makes). 2) inputs and the place. 3) each step with its cause and its condition. 4) what breaks when a step fails. 5) the whole run once more at speed. 6) recap as a flow.
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the whole in context. 2) zoom into each part in a fixed path (outside to inside). 3) function of each part tied to its shape. 4) how the parts work together. 5) labelled recap.
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the overview tree first: the basis of division and every member named. 2) every member in the same slots: layer and shape, why it is named so, its special feature, its function with its cause, where it is found by a zoom from the organ, its consequence. 3) the members compared side by side, the most confused pair named directly. 4) a memory trick for the family.
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what is common. 2) criteria one at a time, both sides together. 3) the reason behind each difference. 4) the most confused pair named directly. 5) difference table as recap.
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the period and its atmosphere. 2) events in order with their causes. 3) the people and their choices. 4) the turning point. 5) what changed after. 6) timeline recap.
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the effect students can see. 2) the cause. 3) each link of the chain with its mechanism. 4) the evidence. 5) the exception or limit. 6) the chain as recap.
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) the fact in one line. 2) the number shown to scale against something familiar. 3) where it comes from (book or outside, dated). 4) what it changes or proves. 5) a formula built term by term when there is one.
- figure · Figure: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only). Required questions: what (kya), which (kaun). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) what the figure is and why it is here. 2) a reading path across it (labels in order). 3) the one thing to remember from it. 4) link back to the text it explains.
- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).
  Teaching pattern: 1) a concrete example first. 2) the book's definition word by word. 3) a non-example that tests the boundary. 4) where the term is used next in the chapter.

How BIE talks to you: every request is a task card (JSON) followed by its source. The card names the unit, its parts with their content type and required questions, the ids of the rules above that apply, the output, the ids you must cover and the context. The card is BIE's instruction; the source is the material.
For a write_script card:
- card.parts are this video's parts: each has item ids, one content type and the questions it must answer. The source gives every item's
  full content and its teacher questions with ids ("p003-i4#q2") and answers from BIE's chapter map; teach from them.
- card.coverage.must_cover lists every item this video must teach: each must be in covers_item_ids of a beat that really explains it.
  may_skip lists items you may leave out (not teachable). card.context.map_slice shows the related concepts for context only.
How to fill the JSON:
- notes: brief notes for the reviewer: what this video is about, the key questions it must answer, your main decisions (order,
  hook, analogy, where prerequisites are taught) with a reason each, what is uncertain.
- title: the video title in the learner language.
- parts: one entry per card part, with the universal frame of that part (S3-01), each in one or two lines of clear English for BIE:
  process (what happens or what the thing does), how (how it works or happens), when (when, in what order, under which timing),
  conditions (what must be true for it, or what changes it), atmosphere (the setting and situation a student should picture). Write
  "n/a: " and the reason only where a question truly does not apply to that part. skipped_steps = the teaching-pattern steps of this
  part you leave out because there is nothing real to say for them, each with the reason ([] when every step is done); at most half
  of a pattern, never a step that has something real; BIE's code records the reason.
- beats: the whole video in order. beat_id "b1", "b2" ...; part_id = the card part this beat teaches ("" for the opening hook, a
  prerequisite taught first, a transition or the final recap); step = the number of the teaching-pattern step of that part's content type
  that this beat performs (see the content types above; 0 when part_id is "" and for an exam-question part, whose type is "none");
  the steps of a part's pattern appear in order, except the ones skipped with a reason; a classification part follows the family
  pattern: the overview tree first, then every member in the same slots (layer and shape → why it is named so → its special feature
  → its function with its cause → where it is found, by a zoom from the organ → its consequence), then the comparison, then a memory
  trick; one recap per part and one closing recap for the video, never two recaps of the same thing;
  purpose (hook, prerequisite, explain, example, analogy, story, compare, process_walkthrough, misconception, exam_tip,
  question_to_student, recap, transition); say = the exact spoken words, one to four complete spoken sentences in Navin's Hinglish
  (S2-04), the way a teacher speaks to one student, never clipped note-style lines ("Irregular walls. Kaisi? Irregular." is a teacher's
  beat; "Location: kidney tubules, glandular ducts." is a note):
  mixed script: Hindi words in Devanagari, English words (above all the book's technical terms, spelled as the book spells them) in
  Roman, as in "आज हम tissue के बारे में पढ़ेंगे"; brackets only after a genuinely difficult Hindi word (see "Brackets" below; the
  screen shows the bracket and the voice says "सतह, यानी surface"); never write an English term in Devanagari or a Hindi word in Roman;
  numbers as digits; addressed to one student; covers_item_ids = the item ids this beat really explains; answers = the teacher question
  ids this beat really answers; on_screen = what the student should see while hearing it (for the director); basis = book, outside or
  mixed.
Opening the book (S2-07; BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher, never a reader of the line): every new
topic (every concept and every prerequisite) opens with a question about something the learner can see, then the name. After any
book line, the beat carries at least one of: the term opened ("yaani" + its plain meaning + one everyday image), the why from a need or
a problem, or an example or place by a zoom from the organ. The source gives every item's unpack from Section 1 (its terms, why chain,
example, consequence, visual verb) and the locked explanations: speak them, in your own teacher's words, at the depth of the level
profile below. BIE's code sends back a beat whose English words are the book's and that opens nothing ("dohraav pakad"), a clipped
sentence without a verb, a topic that opens without a question, and a second recap of the same thing.
Real-world application (S2-08; Navin, 27 October 2026: "economic concepts ko real world mein apply karke samjhao"): for an economics
definition, cause_effect or process item the source gives the real_world_example Section 1 chose (place, actors, goods, numbers before
→ after, the steps with their mechanism links, the naming sentence, the real-life link). Run that example FIRST, in beats that cover
the item and carry its numbers as digits ("dukaan mein chini ke 3 packet, ₹50 ka ek; kal 2 khareedar, aaj 12"), walking the mechanism
step by step (purpose story or example); only then the beat that names the term ("isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain"), then
the book's definition, then the real-life link. The opening question of such a topic asks about the situation, not the term. BIE's
code sends back a script whose naming beat comes before the example beats, or whose example beats carry none of the numbers.
Time (S2-01): the source gives this video's narration time; BIE's code counts the spoken words (130 a minute) and the script must stay
within it. Win the time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content: every item in must_cover is taught and every
teacher question whose basis is "book" is answered; questions answered from outside the book are used only where they help and the
time allows.
Prerequisites (S2-03): in a topic video they were already taught in the prerequisite video; remind of one in at most 2 beats (purpose
"prerequisite"). In the prerequisite video (card parts "pre1", "pre2" ...) teach each prerequisite simply, with an everyday example, in
the order given: part_id = the prerequisite id, step 0, covers_item_ids = the prerequisite ids the beat teaches, answers [].
A beat introduces at most a few new items: BIE's code measures the load of every beat (0.4 per new item plus 1 per 50 spoken words, at
most 1.8), so a beat holds at most about 70 spoken words with one new item, 50 with two and 30 with three; split longer beats. Reply
with the JSON object only.

Level profile: UPSC / State PCS (level_profiles.json; learners: UPSC and State PCS aspirants, often from arts backgrounds, who need understanding more than technical vocabulary).
- Terms: fewer technical terms: only the ones the exam asks, each opened with its plain meaning and an everyday image; a term the exam never asks is explained in words, not named.
- Why: 2 step(s); a two-step why from a need the learner can feel, then its link to daily life, health or governance.
- Where found: the main places, each linked to something the learner already knows (a disease, a food, a news item).
- Exam beats: the PYQ pattern: how this fact has been asked (statement combinations, 'which is correct', odd one out) and the wording that traps.
- Links: daily life, health, the news and earlier chapters of the same paper.

How real teachers open a book line (teacher example bank 2026-10-27.1; use these ways, in your own words):
- Open with a question on something visible (every new topic and every new family member): Skin aur stomach, kidney ke upar ek outer layer hai ki nahi? Yeh kis se bani hai? — phir naam: epithelial tissue.
- One everyday image per shape or function (every term that names a shape, a layer or a job): Chaadar bichhi ho to bistar bacha rehta hai = protective sheet. Cube wala game, har side barabar = cuboidal. Building ka pillar = columnar. Farsh ki tiles = squamous, isliye tessellated bhi kehte hain.
- The word root where it helps (a term whose parts carry its meaning): Epi yaani upar; epithelium yaani upar ki parat. Slender yaani long aur narrow.
- Why starts from a need (every why step): Pet mein HCl banta hai, isliye andar ek lining chahiye jo khud na jale. Cells bahar ki taraf hain, tootne ka chance zyada, isliye regeneration zyada.
- Contrast with the neighbour (members of one family, and what the exam confuses): Simple epithelium ka kaam protection nahi, woh compound ka hai. Zyada layers = pathogen andar nahi aata.
- Ask and repeat the key word (the one word the learner must keep): Irregular walls. Kaisi? Irregular.
- Exam memory beats by level (after the understanding, by the level profile): Yaad rakhna: brush border PCT mein. Doosre naam: pavement, tessellated. M2B = muscle to bone = tendon, B2B = bone to bone = ligament.
- Link to something already known (a new place or a new structure): Peritoneum, jaise lungs ke aas-paas pleura aur heart ke aas-paas pericardium: wahi kaam, pet ke andar.
- Meaning with two or three real examples (an abstract word in the book): Sensory perception yaani pehchanna: thanda lagna, dard hona, pressure mehsoos karna.
- Open the book's adjective (Navin's example) (a book line names a kind of surface, job or place without saying what it is): Book: 'epithelium absorptive aur secretive surfaces par milta hai'. Teacher: absorptive surface yaani jahan cheezein andar li jaati hain, jaise aant khane ke poshak tatva sokhti hai; secretive yaani jahan cells kuch bana kar bahar chhodte hain, jaise glands enzyme ya juice. Aur epithelium wahan kyon? Kyunki ek patli, lagi hui parat hi cheezon ko paar jaane de sakti hai aur bana kar chhod sakti hai.
- Apply it in the real world first, then name it (Navin's sugar shop) (every economics concept (a definition, a cause-and-effect chain, a process): the example runs before the term is named): Ek kirana shop mein chini ke 3 packet hain, ₹50 ka ek. Kal 2 khareedar aaye the, aaj 12 aa gaye; sab ko chini chahiye par packet 3 hi hain. Dukandar daam ₹65 kar deta hai; ab sirf 3 log kharid paate hain, baaki 9 khaali haath. Zyada log, utna hi maal, isliye daam upar. Isliye ise demand-pull inflation kehte hain. Phir book ki definition. Phir: yahi aap Diwali se pehle sabzi mandi mein dekhte hain.

Brackets (word list 2026-10-27.2): use everyday spoken Hindi freely, without brackets (मुख्य, वापस, बराबर, आसपास, इस्तेमाल, करके, जिससे ...). Only a genuinely difficult Hindi word (formal, literary or technical) gets its English word in brackets right after it, for example "सतह (surface)", "घर्षण (friction)", "सघन (dense)"; better still, use the book's English term or a simpler Hindi word. Never put a bracket inside an idiom or a fixed phrase: "आम तौर पर", not "आम तौर (usually) पर"; "नहीं के बराबर", not "नहीं के बराबर (equal to)". BIE's code removes a bracket after an everyday word and asks for one only after a Hindi word it does not know as everyday.

Video v13: RuPay, e-RUPI और merchant को मिलने वाली रकम
Goal: Learner RuPay card types, domestic role और overseas links समझेगा; e-RUPI की beneficiary–purpose restrictions और MDR के payer, recipients तथा gross–net calculation को अलग कर सकेगा।
Opening hook: Customer ने पूरा payment किया, फिर merchant के account में उससे कम रकम क्यों आ सकती है?
Story or analogy: पहले card family का overview और types की समान criteria पर comparison होगी। फिर purpose-bound voucher की situation से e-RUPI समझेंगे। Supplied 2% MDR example में gross amount से fee और net receipt निकालकर fee distribution के participants जोड़ेंगे; voucher को Digital Rupee या खुली cash payment नहीं मानेंगे।
Planned minutes: 9
Narration time (S2-01): 8.1-10.7 minutes, about 1053-1391 spoken words (BIE counts 130 words a minute)
Prerequisites already taught in the prerequisite video (remind of one in at most 2 beats): Purchases, prices, debts and payments due later; Bank balances, deposits, loans and interest; Denominations, monetary arithmetic, percentages and minimum–maximum limits; Purchasing power, inflation, scarcity and liquidity; Central bank, commercial bank, government treasury and bank-to-bank settlement; Foreign currencies, exchange rates, reserves and demand–supply changes; Chronological reading: BCE/CE, centuries, dynasties and law versus implementation dates; Digital instructions, identity authentication, ledgers and payment interfaces
Open every book line (S2-07): a question about something the learner can see, then the name; every term opened: its plain meaning with 'yaani' and one everyday image (the word root where it helps); the why, starting from a need or a problem, one link at a time; an example or the place, by a zoom from the organ or the thing the learner knows; the consequence: what follows, and the link to the previous or the next idea; the contrast: what it is not, and what the exam confuses it with; the memory beat by level: the exam's 'yaad rakhna', the other names, the trick.

notes.about: The unit connects RuPay cards and overseas use with restricted e-RUPI vouchers and merchant-side card-payment fees. Coverage and MDR arithmetic are largely sound, but teaching-pattern and documentation requirements remain unmet.

problems.problem: The maker's notes are null. The required account of the unit, teaching decisions, reasons and uncertainties is missing.
problems.fix: Populate notes with the unit's role, key questions, decisions with reasons, and uncertainties. This requires no narration time.

problems.problem: Debit, credit and prepaid are named before concrete examples run. Their treatment is also uneven: only prepaid receives an everyday image, and the promised common slots are not actually developed for every member.
problems.fix: Replace these compressed definitions with three parallel numerical spending examples before naming each type. For each, show where funds sit, what happens when spending occurs, when money is supplied or repaid, and the consequence. Then compare debit with prepaid and retain the memory trick. Recover time from repeated voucher recaps.

problems.problem: The vaccination example, restricted-use conclusion and issuance-versus-acceptance distinction are repeatedly re-taught. These are duplicate recaps, not separate explanatory advances, contrary to the explicit no-repetition requirement.
problems.fix: Run the vaccination story once, attaching the definition, comparisons and restrictions at the relevant moments. Keep the required fast process run and flow recap brief and distinct. Teach country facts once and use the figure pass specifically for visual reading. Reallocate the saved narration to parallel card-type examples.

problems.problem: The source/provenance step is skipped because no independent dated source exists, although that does not justify omitting attribution for supplied facts. In particular, the unusual 'world's seventh payment gateway' wording is delivered without clearly identifying it as the supplied source's terminology, despite the subsequent technical correction.
problems.fix: Use a non-spoken source annotation identifying the supplied source for milestones and its 'seventh payment gateway' wording. Keep the spoken network-versus-gateway clarification. Replace a repetitive recap rather than extending narration.

beats.say: अब approved borrowing limit ₹1,000 है; उससे ₹200 खर्च किए तो unused limit ₹800 और चुकाने वाला उधार ₹200 हुआ। पैसे अपने deposit से नहीं गए; repayment बाद में करनी है।
beats.on_screen: Illustration 2: borrowing limit ₹1,000 → ₹800 available; ₹200 debt incurred, repay later.

beats.say: यह credit card है: approved limit से उधार खर्च, भुगतान बाद में; जैसे उधारी का हिसाब चुकाना।
beats.on_screen: Reveal credit: borrowing facility → purchase → later repayment.

beats.say: तीसरे card में पहले ₹1,000 value load की; ₹200 खर्च करने पर loaded balance ₹800 बचा। खर्च उसी भरी value से हुआ, जैसे recharge balance; और इस्तेमाल के लिए आगे value फिर load करनी पड़ सकती है।
beats.on_screen: Illustration 3: load ₹1,000 first → spend ₹200 → ₹800 stored value remains; no borrowing created.

beats.say: यह prepaid card है: पहले payment करके value भरना, फिर उसी से खर्च करना।
beats.on_screen: Reveal prepaid: load first → spend stored value.

beats.say: Debit और prepaid में अपना पैसा है, लेकिन जगह अलग: linked bank account या पहले loaded value। Credit में उधार है; RuPay brand इनमें से किसी एक funding source तक सीमित नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Compare identical slots: funds location | ₹200 spending effect | funding/repayment timing | consequence. Highlight debit versus prepaid.

beats.say: याद रखने का तरीका: debit अपना account, credit उधार, prepaid पहले load। ‘RuPay केवल debit है’ इसलिए गलत है।
beats.on_screen: Debit—account; credit—borrow; prepaid—load first.

beats.say: इन flags के साथ dates और machines के symbols क्यों हैं? Overseas inset अलग-अलग देशों में RuPay की मौजूदगी को पढ़ने की visual key देता है।
beats.on_screen: Show the six-country inset; highlight flag, country name and associated note as separate reading fields.

beats.say: ऊपर से नीचे हर flag, फिर उसका country name, फिर उसी row का note पढ़िए। Coloured dots पहचान के लिए हैं, payment की direction या मात्रा बताने के लिए नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Trace Bhutan → Nepal → Mauritius → UAE → Singapore → Maldives without repeating country facts. No arrows or quantitative scale.

beats.say: Date ढूँढ़ते समय issuance वाली rows चुनिए: Bhutan और Mauritius। Acceptance वाली row को issuance का प्रमाण मत बनाइए।
beats.on_screen: Highlight issuance rows, with 2020 and 2024 visible but not re-narrated. Issuance ≠ acceptance.

beats.say: इस visual को matching aid समझिए, worldwide coverage की पूरी list नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Read the specific note; do not infer universal acceptance.

beats.say: ₹1,000 की vaccination पक्की करनी हो, cash देना जरूरी है? सरकार आपके account में पैसे डालने के बजाय आपके लिए ₹1,000 voucher SMS या QR Code से भेजती है।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical vaccination: ₹1,000 voucher, not account credit.

beats.say: आप authorised centre पर उसी vaccination के लिए redeem करते हैं। पूरी redemption में unused value ₹1,000 से ₹0 होती है और vaccination 0 से 1।
beats.on_screen: Voucher → specified vaccination; ₹1,000 → ₹0 unused.

beats.say: ₹1,000 यहाँ समझाने के लिए लिया amount है, universal limit या किसी actual scheme का दावा नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical illustration, not a universal voucher limit or reported scheme amount.

beats.say: यही 2021 का e-RUPI है: SMS/QR Code based Prepaid Cashless Electronic Voucher। National Payments Corporation of India, NPCI ने UPI platform पर बनाया; prepaid पहले funded, cashless यानी covered payment में cash नहीं देना।
beats.on_screen: e-RUPI • 2021 • NPCI • UPI platform; unpack prepaid and cashless.

beats.say: Person-specific यानी तय व्यक्ति; purpose-specific यानी तय काम। किसे देना है और किस काम पर इस्तेमाल होगा, अलग checks हैं; एक से दूसरा अपने-आप तय नहीं होता।
beats.on_screen: Two locks: person + purpose.

beats.say: बिना service restriction का account credit इसका non-example है; उसमें voucher वाले 2 locks नहीं हैं।
beats.on_screen: Boundary test: unrestricted account credit fails the voucher definition.

beats.say: Definition की पहचान रखिए: prepaid voucher, तय व्यक्ति और तय service।
beats.on_screen: Definition checkpoint: instrument + beneficiary + purpose.

beats.say: Phone पर app और coupon दोनों दिखें, तो समान हैं? Digital appearance समान है; e-RUPI restrictions वाला gift coupon जैसा है।
beats.on_screen: Common digital form, different functions.

beats.say: App interface है; e-RUPI voucher है, bank transfer या digital currency नहीं। Gift coupon की तुलना में भी intended beneficiary और intended service के locks रहेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Voucher versus app, transfer, currency; retain both locks.

beats.say: SMS उसका delivery तरीका है, instrument की पहचान नहीं; UPI platform भी voucher को bank transfer नहीं बनाता।
beats.on_screen: Delivery medium ≠ instrument; underlying platform ≠ bank transfer.

beats.say: खास trap है e-RUPI बनाम Digital Rupee; gift coupon की analogy भी unrestricted या transferable money नहीं बनाती।
beats.on_screen: Confused pair: restricted voucher ≠ Digital Rupee; do not infer transferability.

beats.say: Comparison में appearance नहीं, काम और restrictions देखकर सही category चुनिए।
beats.on_screen: Difference table: app | bank transfer | currency | restricted voucher.

beats.say: उस ₹1,000 example की सफलता किससे जाँचेंगे? Result vaccination मिलना है, cash balance बढ़ना नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Process audit of the already-shown story: intended outcome = vaccination.

beats.say: इसमें government funding देती है, beneficiary इस्तेमाल करता है और authorised centre service देता है।
beats.on_screen: Freeze the existing story and label sponsor, user and redemption place; do not replay it.

beats.say: Delivery redemption से पहले चाहिए: SMS/QR voucher तय service लेने का funded entitlement पहुँचाता है, खुला account credit नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Annotate the existing flow: delivery precedes redemption; service entitlement rather than unrestricted credit.

beats.say: दूसरी खरीदारी allowed हो जाए, तो intended service तक मदद पहुँचने की guarantee टूट जाएगी।
beats.on_screen: Failure test: removing the purpose lock breaks targeted use.

beats.say: Fast run: सरकार भेजती है, beneficiary पाता है, centre पर service लेता है।
beats.on_screen: One brief animated run through the existing example.

beats.say: Flow में delivery और redemption अलग stages हैं; voucher मिलते ही service मिलना पूरा नहीं होता।
beats.on_screen: Delivery → restricted redemption → intended outcome.

beats.say: सही service हो, लेकिन centre authorised न हो, तो चलेगा? नहीं; purpose के साथ place की condition भी है।
beats.on_screen: Apply a new boundary test: correct service but unauthorised centre → not permitted.

beats.say: ‘Only’ और ‘authorized’ allowed use बताते हैं; ‘not withdraw cash’ redemption को cash-out से अलग रखता है।
beats.on_screen: Evidence annotation on supplied wording: only for vaccination | authorized center | not withdraw cash or spend elsewhere.

beats.say: Allowed use पहचानते समय service और authorised place, दोनों जाँचिए।
beats.on_screen: Permission checklist: service AND place.

beats.say: किराना दुकान पर card से ₹1,000 दिए; seller को कितने मिलेंगे? Illustrated 2% fee में ₹20 कटेंगे, ₹980 पहुँचेंगे।
beats.on_screen: ₹1,000 sale − ₹20 fee = ₹980 receipt.

beats.say: यह Merchant Discount Rate, MDR है: seller की हर card transaction पर acquiring bank को दी जाने वाली fee। Acquirer दुकानदार की तरफ payment acceptance संभालता है।
beats.on_screen: MDR: merchant's acceptance fee to acquirer.

beats.say: Discount customer की price छूट नहीं है। Card acceptance की व्यवस्था की fee से merchant की net receipt कम होती है।
beats.on_screen: Not a price discount; acceptance service fee.

beats.say: Card sale और bank receipt का फर्क MDR समझाता है। अब इसके recipients देखिए।
beats.on_screen: Gross sale versus net receipt.

beats.say: Acquirer को fee दी तो पूरी उसी की? नहीं; payment में कई participants हैं, MDR उनके बीच share होती है।
beats.on_screen: One fee, multiple recipients.

beats.say: Acquiring Bank यानी दुकान को card से पैसे लेने की व्यवस्था देने वाला bank; Issuing Bank यानी आपको card देने वाला bank। Card Network और जहाँ लागू हो Payment Service Provider/Gateway भी fee share करते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Shop's card-acceptance arrangement → acquirer; your card → issuer; network and applicable provider also share MDR.

beats.say: Acquirer acceptance संभालता है, issuer card देता है, RuPay जैसे network messages जोड़ते हैं। Gateway/provider processing का interface दे सकता है, जैसे online checkout।
beats.on_screen: Participant roles; networks: RuPay, Visa, Mastercard.

beats.say: ये roles मिलकर payment चलाते हैं; collection point अकेला final recipient नहीं। Individual allocation percentages दिए नहीं गए हैं।
beats.on_screen: Collection ≠ sole retention; allocations unspecified.

beats.say: Acquirer, issuer, network और applicable provider याद रखें। Shared का मतलब equal shares नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Labelled participant recap without allocation percentages.

beats.say: MDR का direct payer कौन? Merchant, customer नहीं; खरीदारी का payment अलग है।
beats.on_screen: MDR payer: merchant.

beats.say: Customer ₹1,000 देता है, ₹1,020 नहीं। ₹20 merchant की तरफ कटते हैं; उसे ₹980 मिलते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Deduction on merchant side.

beats.say: Direct payer merchant है। Costs को prices में गिनना अलग economic सवाल है; उससे direct obligation नहीं बदलती।
beats.on_screen: Direct payer ≠ ultimate economic incidence.

beats.say: इन 3 boxes में payment से fee कैसे अलग दिखती है? Figure gross payment, net receipt और fee-sharing जोड़ता है।
beats.on_screen: Customer → Merchant → Banks & Payment Network.

beats.say: बाएँ Customer से Merchant तक ₹1,000 arrow देखिए, जैसे पूरा bill चुकाना। यह gross purchase payment है, fee नहीं; percentage इसी base पर लगेगा।
beats.on_screen: Trace buyer → ₹1,000 → seller; gross base.

beats.say: बीच का Merchant seller है: payment अंदर, MDR shared arrow बाहर। जैसे मिली payment से खर्च अलग रखना, total ₹20 recipients की ओर जाते हैं; ₹980 बचते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Incoming gross; outgoing total fee; retained net.

beats.say: दाएँ grouped box कोई एक organisation नहीं: acquirer, issuer, RuPay/Visa/Mastercard जैसे networks और applicable provider समझिए। Individual shares नहीं दिखाए गए।
beats.on_screen: Expand grouped recipients; no equal-share assumption.

beats.say: 2% rate है, ₹980 receipt है। हर ₹100 पर ₹2 कटते हैं, इसलिए ₹1,000 को 2 से multiply करके 100 से divide करें तो ₹20 fee मिलती है। ₹1,000 से ₹20 घटाएँ तो ₹980 बचते हैं।
beats.on_screen: ₹1,000 × 2 ÷ 100 = ₹20 fee; ₹1,000 − ₹20 = ₹980 receipt. Distinguish rate from rupees.

beats.say: Figure में ₹1,000 gross = ₹980 net + ₹20 total fee। 2% illustrative है, universal rate नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Gross = net + total fee; illustrative rate.

beats.say: याद रखिए: RuPay network है, e-RUPI restricted voucher है, MDR merchant-paid fee है।
beats.on_screen: Network | restricted voucher | merchant fee.

beats.say: आपने card से ₹1,000 दिए, दुकानदार को ₹980 क्यों मिले? पहले card, voucher और fee का फर्क समझिए।
beats.on_screen: ₹1,000 paid → ₹980 received?

beats.say: Card पर RuPay देखा है? Rupee और Payment के शुरुआती टुकड़े जोड़िए, जैसे नाम की puzzle: RuPay। यह पैसों की equation नहीं; NPCI ने इसे 2012 में launch किया।
beats.on_screen: Join word fragments: Rupee + Payment → RuPay; NPCI, 2012.

beats.say: Jan Dhan account के पैसे branch जाए बिना कैसे इस्तेमाल करें? PMJDY के साथ free RuPay debit card मिलता है। Free issuance का मतलब credit या हर transaction free नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Account access beyond branch → free RuPay debit card.

beats.say: UPI दिखे तो deposit ही खर्च होगा? RuPay Credit Cards का UPI linkage बड़ा innovation है: interface UPI, लेकिन funding credit से, यानी उधार से।
beats.on_screen: UPI interface ≠ credit funding source.

beats.say: विदेश में card मिलना और चलना समान हैं? Bhutan: पहला overseas issuance milestone 2020, साथ में ATM और merchant acceptance। Mauritius: issuance 2024 में शुरू, यानी नया card देना।
beats.on_screen: Bhutan: 2020 issuance + acceptance. Mauritius: 2024 issuance.

beats.say: Nepal और Maldives में कहाँ चलेगा? दोनों में ATM और PoS acceptance है: cash निकालने की machine और दुकान का payment counter। इन entries में issuance year नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Nepal and Maldives: ATM + point-of-sale acceptance; no issuance year.

beats.say: United Arab Emirates और Singapore में क्या समान है? ATM और merchant-terminal acceptance, यानी cash machine और दुकान के card reader पर इस्तेमाल; issuance date नहीं दी गई।
beats.on_screen: UAE and Singapore: ATM + merchant-terminal acceptance.

beats.say: ये dates issuance की हैं, total usage की नहीं।
beats.on_screen: NON-SPOKEN PROVENANCE: supplied BIE source, p015-i14: Bhutan overseas issuance milestone, 2020; p015-i16: Mauritius issuance began, 2024. Supplied source only; no independent statistical series provided.

beats.say: Card type, country की activity और year अलग पहचानिए।
beats.on_screen: Three separate recall fields: card type | activity | date. Non-spoken provenance: supplied BIE source, p015-i7, i11–i19; dates are supplied milestones, not independently updated statistics.

beats.say: Card पर अलग brands क्यों दिखते हैं? RuPay, Mastercard, Visa और China का Union Pay समान card-payment role वाली व्यवस्थाएँ हैं।
beats.on_screen: RuPay | Mastercard | Visa | Union Pay.

beats.say: RuPay Indian domestic payment system है; fees दूसरी companies से कम बताई जाती हैं। Numerical schedule नहीं है; lower fee, zero fee नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Indian origin; lower fees, unquantified.

beats.say: Domestic origin है, domestic-only use नहीं। ‘7th’ से size, transaction volume या quality की ranking नहीं निकलती; उसके लिए metric चाहिए।
beats.on_screen: Non-spoken source annotation: supplied source p015-i8 describes RuPay as 'world’s 7th payment gateway'; no ranking criterion or operational comparison is supplied. Technical clarification follows: card network ≠ payment gateway.

beats.say: Technical फर्क रखिए: card network participating banks को जोड़ता है। Gateway merchant के payment interface से जानकारी processing की ओर भेजता है; दोनों roles अलग हैं।
beats.on_screen: Network: bank connections. Gateway: interface-to-processing information.

beats.say: समान payment role, Indian origin और lower fees याद रखें; exact savings नहीं दी गई हैं।
beats.on_screen: Table: common role | domestic origin | qualitative fees; detailed operational differences unspecified.

beats.say: एक जैसे दिखने वाले cards में खर्च का पैसा कहाँ से आता है? Family के 3 रास्ते समझिए: account के पैसे, उधार की limit और पहले भरी value; फिर इनके नाम जोड़ेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Funding tree: linked account | approved borrowing | preloaded value. Reveal card-type names only after each example.

beats.say: आपके bank account में ₹1,000 हैं; दुकान पर card से ₹200 खर्च किए। Payment के लिए उसी account के पैसे इस्तेमाल हुए, balance ₹800 बचा; पैसे पहले आपके थे, बाद में उधार चुकाना नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Illustration 1: linked bank account ₹1,000 → ₹800 after ₹200 purchase; no borrowing repayment.

beats.say: यह debit card है: linked account से अपने पैसे खर्च हुए, जैसे अपने बटुए से देना।
beats.on_screen: Reveal debit: linked account → purchase; own money supplied before spending.

beats.say: अब approved borrowing limit ₹1,000 है; उससे ₹200 खर्च किए तो unused limit ₹800 और चुकाने वाला उधार ₹200 हुआ। पैसे अपने deposit से नहीं गए; repayment बाद में करनी है।
beats.on_screen: Illustration 2: borrowing limit ₹1,000 → ₹800 available; ₹200 debt incurred, repay later.

beats.say: यह credit card है: approved limit से उधार खर्च, भुगतान बाद में; जैसे उधारी का हिसाब चुकाना।
beats.on_screen: Reveal credit: borrowing facility → purchase → later repayment.

beats.say: तीसरे card में पहले ₹1,000 value load की; ₹200 खर्च करने पर loaded balance ₹800 बचा। खर्च उसी भरी value से हुआ, जैसे recharge balance; और इस्तेमाल के लिए आगे value फिर load करनी पड़ सकती है।
beats.on_screen: Illustration 3: load ₹1,000 first → spend ₹200 → ₹800 stored value remains; no borrowing created.

beats.say: यह prepaid card है: पहले payment करके value भरना, फिर उसी से खर्च करना।
beats.on_screen: Reveal prepaid: load first → spend stored value.

beats.say: Debit और prepaid में अपना पैसा है, लेकिन जगह अलग: linked bank account या पहले loaded value। Credit में उधार है; RuPay brand इनमें से किसी एक funding source तक सीमित नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Compare identical slots: funds location | ₹200 spending effect | funding/repayment timing | consequence. Highlight debit versus prepaid.

beats.say: याद रखने का तरीका: debit अपना account, credit उधार, prepaid पहले load। ‘RuPay केवल debit है’ इसलिए गलत है।
beats.on_screen: Debit—account; credit—borrow; prepaid—load first.

beats.say: इन flags के साथ dates और machines के symbols क्यों हैं? Overseas inset अलग-अलग देशों में RuPay की मौजूदगी को पढ़ने की visual key देता है।
beats.on_screen: Show the six-country inset; highlight flag, country name and associated note as separate reading fields.

beats.say: ऊपर से नीचे flag, country और उसी row का note पढ़िए। Dots पहचान हैं, direction या मात्रा नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Trace Bhutan → Nepal → Mauritius → UAE → Singapore → Maldives without repeating country facts. No arrows or quantitative scale.

beats.say: Date ढूँढ़ते समय issuance वाली rows चुनिए: Bhutan और Mauritius। Acceptance वाली row को issuance का प्रमाण मत बनाइए।
beats.on_screen: Highlight issuance rows, with 2020 and 2024 visible but not re-narrated. Issuance ≠ acceptance.

beats.say: इस visual को matching aid समझिए, worldwide coverage की पूरी list नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Read the specific note; do not infer universal acceptance.

beats.say: ₹1,000 की vaccination पक्की करनी हो, cash देना जरूरी है? सरकार आपके account में पैसे डालने के बजाय आपके लिए ₹1,000 voucher SMS या QR Code से भेजती है।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical vaccination: ₹1,000 voucher, not account credit.

beats.say: आप authorised centre पर उसी vaccination के लिए redeem करते हैं। पूरी redemption में unused value ₹1,000 से ₹0 होती है और vaccination 0 से 1।
beats.on_screen: Voucher → specified vaccination; ₹1,000 → ₹0 unused.

beats.say: ₹1,000 यहाँ समझाने के लिए लिया amount है, universal limit या किसी actual scheme का दावा नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical illustration, not a universal voucher limit or reported scheme amount.

beats.say: यही 2021 का e-RUPI है: SMS/QR Code based Prepaid Cashless Electronic Voucher। National Payments Corporation of India, NPCI ने UPI platform पर बनाया; prepaid पहले funded, cashless यानी covered payment में cash नहीं देना।
beats.on_screen: e-RUPI • 2021 • NPCI • UPI platform; unpack prepaid and cashless.

beats.say: Person-specific यानी तय व्यक्ति; purpose-specific यानी तय काम। किसे देना है और किस काम पर इस्तेमाल होगा, अलग checks हैं; एक से दूसरा अपने-आप तय नहीं होता।
beats.on_screen: Two locks: person + purpose.

beats.say: Unrestricted account credit इसका non-example है; उसमें ये 2 locks नहीं हैं।
beats.on_screen: Boundary test: unrestricted account credit fails the voucher definition.

beats.say: Definition की पहचान रखिए: prepaid voucher, तय व्यक्ति और तय service।
beats.on_screen: Definition checkpoint: instrument + beneficiary + purpose.

beats.say: Phone पर app और coupon दोनों दिखें, तो समान हैं? Digital appearance समान है; e-RUPI restrictions वाला gift coupon जैसा है।
beats.on_screen: Common digital form, different functions.

beats.say: App interface है; e-RUPI voucher है, bank transfer या digital currency नहीं। Gift coupon की तुलना में भी intended beneficiary और intended service के locks रहेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Voucher versus app, transfer, currency; retain both locks.

beats.say: SMS delivery है, currency होने का प्रमाण नहीं; UPI platform भी इसे bank transfer नहीं बनाता।
beats.on_screen: Delivery medium ≠ instrument; underlying platform ≠ bank transfer.

beats.say: खास trap है e-RUPI बनाम Digital Rupee; gift coupon की analogy भी unrestricted या transferable money नहीं बनाती।
beats.on_screen: Confused pair: restricted voucher ≠ Digital Rupee; do not infer transferability.

beats.say: Comparison में appearance नहीं, काम और restrictions देखकर सही category चुनिए।
beats.on_screen: Difference table: app | bank transfer | currency | restricted voucher.

beats.say: ₹1,000 example का result क्या है? Vaccination मिलना, cash balance बढ़ना नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Process audit of the already-shown story: intended outcome = vaccination.

beats.say: इसमें government funding देती है, beneficiary इस्तेमाल करता है और authorised centre service देता है।
beats.on_screen: Freeze the existing story and label sponsor, user and redemption place; do not replay it.

beats.say: पहले SMS/QR voucher पहुँचता है, फिर redemption होता है; funded entitlement मिलता है, खुला account credit नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Annotate the existing flow: delivery precedes redemption; service entitlement rather than unrestricted credit.

beats.say: दूसरी खरीदारी allowed हो जाए, तो intended service तक मदद पहुँचने की guarantee टूट जाएगी।
beats.on_screen: Failure test: removing the purpose lock breaks targeted use.

beats.say: Fast run: सरकार भेजती है, beneficiary पाता है, centre पर service लेता है।
beats.on_screen: One brief animated run through the existing example.

beats.say: Delivery के बाद restricted redemption चाहिए; voucher मिलना service मिलना नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Delivery → restricted redemption → intended outcome.

beats.say: सही service हो, लेकिन centre authorised न हो, तो चलेगा? नहीं; purpose के साथ place की condition भी है।
beats.on_screen: Apply a new boundary test: correct service but unauthorised centre → not permitted.

beats.say: ‘Only’ और ‘authorized’ allowed use बताते हैं; ‘not withdraw cash’ redemption को cash-out से अलग रखता है।
beats.on_screen: Evidence annotation on supplied wording: only for vaccination | authorized center | not withdraw cash or spend elsewhere.

beats.say: Allowed use पहचानते समय service और authorised place, दोनों जाँचिए।
beats.on_screen: Permission checklist: service AND place.

beats.say: किराना दुकान पर card से ₹1,000 दिए; seller को कितने मिलेंगे? Illustrated 2% fee में ₹20 कटेंगे, ₹980 पहुँचेंगे।
beats.on_screen: ₹1,000 sale − ₹20 fee = ₹980 receipt.

beats.say: यह Merchant Discount Rate, MDR है: seller की हर card transaction पर acquiring bank को दी जाने वाली fee। Acquirer दुकानदार की तरफ payment acceptance संभालता है।
beats.on_screen: MDR: merchant's acceptance fee to acquirer.

beats.say: Discount customer की price छूट नहीं है। Card acceptance की व्यवस्था की fee से merchant की net receipt कम होती है।
beats.on_screen: Not a price discount; acceptance service fee.

beats.say: Card sale और bank receipt का फर्क MDR समझाता है। अब इसके recipients देखिए।
beats.on_screen: Gross sale versus net receipt.

beats.say: Acquirer को fee दी तो पूरी उसी की? नहीं; payment में कई participants हैं, MDR उनके बीच share होती है।
beats.on_screen: One fee, multiple recipients.

beats.say: Acquiring Bank यानी दुकान को card से पैसे लेने की व्यवस्था देने वाला bank; Issuing Bank यानी आपको card देने वाला bank। Card Network और जहाँ लागू हो Payment Service Provider/Gateway भी fee share करते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Shop's card-acceptance arrangement → acquirer; your card → issuer; network and applicable provider also share MDR.

beats.say: Acquirer acceptance संभालता है, issuer card देता है, RuPay जैसे network messages जोड़ते हैं। Gateway/provider processing का interface दे सकता है, जैसे online checkout।
beats.on_screen: Participant roles; networks: RuPay, Visa, Mastercard.

beats.say: मिलकर payment चलाने वाले participants fee बाँटते हैं; collection point पूरी fee नहीं रखता। Individual percentages नहीं दिए हैं।
beats.on_screen: Collection ≠ sole retention; allocations unspecified.

beats.say: Acquirer, issuer, network और applicable provider याद रखें। Shared का मतलब equal shares नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Labelled participant recap without allocation percentages.

beats.say: MDR का direct payer कौन? Merchant, customer नहीं; खरीदारी का payment अलग है।
beats.on_screen: MDR payer: merchant.

beats.say: Customer ₹1,000 देता है, ₹1,020 नहीं। ₹20 merchant की तरफ कटते हैं; उसे ₹980 मिलते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Deduction on merchant side.

beats.say: Direct payer merchant है। Costs को prices में गिनना अलग economic सवाल है; उससे direct obligation नहीं बदलती।
beats.on_screen: Direct payer ≠ ultimate economic incidence.

beats.say: ये 3 boxes क्या जोड़ते हैं? Customer का gross payment, merchant की net receipt और participants की fee-sharing।
beats.on_screen: Customer → Merchant → Banks & Payment Network.

beats.say: बाएँ Customer से Merchant तक ₹1,000 arrow देखिए, जैसे पूरा bill चुकाना। यह gross purchase payment है, fee नहीं; percentage इसी base पर लगेगा।
beats.on_screen: Trace buyer → ₹1,000 → seller; gross base.

beats.say: बीच का Merchant seller है: payment अंदर, MDR shared arrow बाहर। जैसे मिली payment से खर्च अलग रखना, total ₹20 recipients की ओर जाते हैं; ₹980 बचते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Incoming gross; outgoing total fee; retained net.

beats.say: दाएँ grouped box कोई एक organisation नहीं: acquirer, issuer, RuPay/Visa/Mastercard जैसे networks और applicable provider समझिए। Individual shares नहीं दिखाए गए।
beats.on_screen: Expand grouped recipients; no equal-share assumption.

beats.say: 2% rate है: हर ₹100 पर ₹2। इसलिए ₹1,000 × 2 ÷ 100 से ₹20 fee मिलती है, ₹2 नहीं। ₹1,000 से ₹20 घटाइए: net receipt ₹980।
beats.on_screen: ₹1,000 × 2 ÷ 100 = ₹20 fee; ₹1,000 − ₹20 = ₹980 receipt. Distinguish rate from rupees.

beats.say: Figure में ₹1,000 gross = ₹980 net + ₹20 total fee। 2% illustrative है, universal rate नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Gross = net + total fee; illustrative rate.

beats.say: याद रखिए: RuPay network है, e-RUPI restricted voucher है, MDR merchant-paid fee है।
beats.on_screen: Network | restricted voucher | merchant fee.

notes.about: This unit connects RuPay's card network and funding types with restricted e-RUPI vouchers and merchant-paid MDR. Most source content and the numerical mechanisms are taught accurately.

Which overseas facts concern issuance rather than acceptance?
What restricts voucher redemption, and who pays and shares MDR?

decisions.decision: Require the supplied seventh-payment-gateway wording to reach the learner with its technical qualification.
decisions.reason: Non-spoken provenance does not replace teaching a mandatory source claim.

decisions.decision: Move card-funding examples before the first instructional use of the card-type names.
decisions.reason: The later examples are sound, but the earlier beats already introduce those concepts.

The prerequisite video and full chapter plan are not supplied, so their execution cannot be independently verified.

problems.problem: The narration mentions an unexplained ‘7th’, while the complete mandatory claim—world's seventh payment gateway—is confined to non-spoken provenance. Learners are not actually taught what that ordinal describes or why the supplied terminology needs qualification.
problems.fix: Replace the dangling ordinal sentence with a learner-facing explanation of the supplied description, immediately distinguishing card networks from gateways and rejecting a size ranking without a metric. Cut the overlapping b13 recap to make room.

problems.problem: Debit and credit are introduced and used instructionally before their numerical examples. The later example-before-name sequence therefore does not satisfy the first-introduction requirement.
problems.fix: Move the existing three funding examples and definitions before the Jan Dhan and credit-card/UPI applications. Replace the displaced transition rather than adding narration.

problems.problem: The opening refers to machine symbols in the inset, but the supplied visual description establishes flags, coloured dots and textual notes, not machine symbols.
problems.fix: Ask why dates and acceptance notes accompany the flags, or explicitly identify machine icons as teacher-added aids rather than original visual features.

frame.process: Identify RuPay's origin, domestic applications and overseas milestones.
frame.how: Separate brand construction, card provisions, credit linkage and country-specific activities.
frame.when: Launch in 2012; overseas issuance milestones in 2020 and 2024.
frame.conditions: Acceptance does not imply issuance or universal availability.
frame.atmosphere: A cardholder using an Indian payment network at home and abroad.

skipped_steps.why: There is no formula; the brand-name expression joins words rather than quantities.

frame.process: Compare RuPay with familiar international payment brands.
frame.how: Use function, domestic identity and qualitative fees as separate criteria.
frame.when: When interpreting brand comparisons and fee claims.
frame.conditions: No operational comparison, fee schedule or ranking metric is supplied.
frame.atmosphere: Payment-brand names displayed on cards and checkout counters.

frame.process: Classify RuPay cards by the source of spending funds.
frame.how: Distinguish account money, borrowing and preloaded value.
frame.when: At spending, with repayment later for credit and loading earlier for prepaid.
frame.conditions: The network brand is independent of the funding category.
frame.atmosphere: A bank customer choosing among three card types.

frame.process: Read the overseas RuPay inset.
frame.how: Follow six country entries vertically and distinguish issuance from acceptance.
frame.when: When matching country names to activities and dates.
frame.conditions: Dots and flags have no quantitative scale or flow meaning.
frame.atmosphere: A six-country visual reference for overseas RuPay presence.

frame.process: Define a prepaid electronic voucher restricted to a person and service.
frame.how: Begin with the ₹1,000 vaccination illustration, then unpack the definition.
frame.when: Value is funded before redemption for the intended service.
frame.conditions: Only the intended beneficiary and intended service qualify.
frame.atmosphere: A beneficiary receives an SMS or QR voucher for an authorised vaccination centre.

frame.process: Distinguish e-RUPI from apps, transfers, currency and unrestricted coupons.
frame.how: Compare digital appearance with the actual function and restrictions.
frame.when: When identifying a phone-delivered payment instrument.
frame.conditions: Digital delivery and UPI infrastructure do not make the voucher general money.
frame.atmosphere: Several different instruments can appear on the same phone.

frame.process: Trace the hypothetical vaccination voucher from government support to redemption.
frame.how: Send ₹1,000 by voucher and redeem it for the specified vaccination.
frame.when: Funding and delivery precede authorised redemption.
frame.conditions: Cash withdrawal and unrelated spending are excluded.
frame.atmosphere: A hypothetical targeted health-service benefit, not a claimed actual scheme.

frame.process: Identify the allowed and excluded uses of the illustrated voucher.
frame.how: Keep purpose and authorised location together.
frame.when: At attempted redemption.
frame.conditions: Vaccination is allowed; cash withdrawal and other purchases are not.
frame.atmosphere: A beneficiary presenting the voucher at an authorised centre.

skipped_steps.why: This continuation supplies a restriction, not a new quantity requiring scale.
No formula applies to this permitted-use statement.

frame.process: Define the merchant's card-acceptance fee.
frame.how: Deduct the illustrative ₹20 from a ₹1,000 card sale before naming MDR.
frame.when: For a merchant's card transaction.
frame.conditions: The merchant pays the acquiring bank; the example assumes 2%.
frame.atmosphere: A kirana seller comparing the bill value with the amount received.

frame.process: Identify participants sharing the merchant-paid fee.
frame.how: Move from merchant-side acquirer to customer-side issuer, network and applicable provider.
frame.when: Within the card-payment acceptance arrangement.
frame.conditions: Provider or gateway participation is conditional; individual shares are unspecified.
frame.atmosphere: Several institutions cooperate behind one card purchase.

frame.process: Identify the direct payer of MDR.
frame.how: Locate the fee deduction on the merchant's receipt rather than the customer's bill.
frame.when: When distinguishing purchase payment from acceptance fee.
frame.conditions: Direct payment obligation is separate from broader pricing decisions.
frame.atmosphere: Customer pays ₹1,000 while seller retains ₹980 in the example.

skipped_steps.why: This is a payer-identification statement, not a dated statistic.

frame.process: Read gross payment, fee distribution and net merchant receipt.

beats.say: आपने card से ₹1,000 दिए, दुकानदार को ₹980 क्यों मिले? पहले card, voucher और fee का फर्क समझिए।
beats.on_screen: ₹1,000 paid → ₹980 received?

beats.say: Card पर RuPay देखा है? Rupee और Payment के शुरुआती टुकड़े जोड़िए, जैसे नाम की puzzle: RuPay। यह पैसों की equation नहीं; NPCI ने इसे 2012 में launch किया।
beats.on_screen: Join word fragments: Rupee + Payment → RuPay; NPCI, 2012.

beats.say: विदेश में card मिलना और चलना समान हैं? Bhutan: पहला overseas issuance milestone 2020, साथ में ATM और merchant acceptance। Mauritius: issuance 2024 में शुरू, यानी नया card देना।
beats.on_screen: Bhutan: 2020 issuance + acceptance. Mauritius: 2024 issuance.

beats.say: Nepal और Maldives में कहाँ चलेगा? दोनों में ATM और PoS acceptance है: cash निकालने की machine और दुकान का payment counter। इन entries में issuance year नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Nepal and Maldives: ATM + point-of-sale acceptance; no issuance year.

beats.say: United Arab Emirates और Singapore में क्या समान है? ATM और merchant-terminal acceptance, यानी cash machine और दुकान के card reader पर इस्तेमाल; issuance date नहीं दी गई।
beats.on_screen: UAE and Singapore: ATM + merchant-terminal acceptance.

beats.say: ये dates issuance की हैं, total usage की नहीं।
beats.on_screen: NON-SPOKEN PROVENANCE: supplied BIE source, p015-i14: Bhutan overseas issuance milestone, 2020; p015-i16: Mauritius issuance began, 2024. Supplied source only; no independent statistical series provided.

beats.say: Card type, country की activity और year अलग पहचानिए।
beats.on_screen: Three separate recall fields: card type | activity | date. Non-spoken provenance: supplied BIE source, p015-i7, i11–i19; dates are supplied milestones, not independently updated statistics.

beats.say: Card पर अलग brands क्यों दिखते हैं? RuPay, Mastercard, Visa और China का Union Pay समान card-payment role वाली व्यवस्थाएँ हैं।
beats.on_screen: RuPay | Mastercard | Visa | Union Pay.

beats.say: RuPay Indian domestic payment system है; fees दूसरी companies से कम बताई जाती हैं। Numerical schedule नहीं है; lower fee, zero fee नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Indian origin; lower fees, unquantified.

beats.say: RuPay को world's 7th payment gateway कहा गया है। यहाँ gateway शब्द card-payment व्यवस्था के लिए है; technically RuPay card network है। बिना metric के ‘7th’ को size या transaction volume की ranking नहीं मानिए; domestic origin भी domestic-only use नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Supplied description: world's 7th payment gateway. Technical qualification: RuPay is a card network; no size-ranking metric supplied. Domestic origin ≠ domestic-only use.

beats.say: Network banks को जोड़ता है; gateway merchant के payment interface से जानकारी processing की ओर भेजता है। Roles अलग हैं।
beats.on_screen: Card network: connects participating banks. Gateway: routes information from merchant interface toward processing.

beats.say: RuPay domestic है; lower fees का मतलब free नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Comparison recap: similar payment role | Indian domestic origin | lower fees, unquantified. Network ≠ gateway.

beats.say: एक जैसे दिखने वाले cards में खर्च का पैसा कहाँ से आता है? Family के 3 रास्ते समझिए: account के पैसे, उधार की limit और पहले भरी value; फिर इनके नाम जोड़ेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Funding tree: linked account | approved borrowing | preloaded value. Reveal card-type names only after each example.

beats.say: आपके bank account में ₹1,000 हैं; दुकान पर card से ₹200 खर्च किए। Payment के लिए उसी account के पैसे इस्तेमाल हुए, balance ₹800 बचा; पैसे पहले आपके थे, बाद में उधार चुकाना नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Illustration 1: linked bank account ₹1,000 → ₹800 after ₹200 purchase; no borrowing repayment.

beats.say: यह debit card है: linked account से अपने पैसे खर्च हुए, जैसे अपने बटुए से देना।
beats.on_screen: Reveal debit: linked account → purchase; own money supplied before spending.

beats.say: अब approved borrowing limit ₹1,000 है; उससे ₹200 खर्च किए तो unused limit ₹800 और चुकाने वाला उधार ₹200 हुआ। पैसे अपने deposit से नहीं गए; repayment बाद में करनी है।
beats.on_screen: Illustration 2: borrowing limit ₹1,000 → ₹800 available; ₹200 debt incurred, repay later.

beats.say: यह credit card है: approved limit से उधार खर्च, भुगतान बाद में; जैसे उधारी का हिसाब चुकाना।
beats.on_screen: Reveal credit: borrowing facility → purchase → later repayment.

beats.say: तीसरे card में पहले ₹1,000 value load की; ₹200 खर्च करने पर loaded balance ₹800 बचा। खर्च उसी भरी value से हुआ, जैसे recharge balance; और इस्तेमाल के लिए आगे value फिर load करनी पड़ सकती है।
beats.on_screen: Illustration 3: load ₹1,000 first → spend ₹200 → ₹800 stored value remains; no borrowing created.

beats.say: यह prepaid card है: पहले payment करके value भरना, फिर उसी से खर्च करना।
beats.on_screen: Reveal prepaid: load first → spend stored value.

beats.say: Debit और prepaid में अपना पैसा है, लेकिन जगह अलग: linked bank account या पहले loaded value। Credit में उधार है; RuPay brand इनमें से किसी एक funding source तक सीमित नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Compare identical slots: funds location | ₹200 spending effect | funding/repayment timing | consequence. Highlight debit versus prepaid.

beats.say: याद रखने का तरीका: debit अपना account, credit उधार, prepaid पहले load। ‘RuPay केवल debit है’ इसलिए गलत है।
beats.on_screen: Debit—account; credit—borrow; prepaid—load first.

beats.say: Jan Dhan account के पैसे branch जाए बिना कैसे इस्तेमाल करें? PMJDY के साथ free RuPay debit card मिलता है। Free issuance का मतलब credit या हर transaction free नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Account access beyond branch → free RuPay debit card.

beats.say: UPI दिखे तो deposit ही खर्च होगा? RuPay Credit Cards का UPI linkage बड़ा innovation है: interface UPI, लेकिन funding credit से, यानी उधार से।
beats.on_screen: UPI interface ≠ credit funding source.

beats.say: इन flags के साथ dates और machines के symbols क्यों हैं? Overseas inset अलग-अलग देशों में RuPay की मौजूदगी को पढ़ने की visual key देता है।
beats.on_screen: Show the six-country inset; highlight flag, country name and associated note as separate reading fields.

beats.say: ऊपर से नीचे flag, country और उसी row का note पढ़िए। Dots पहचान हैं, direction या मात्रा नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Trace Bhutan → Nepal → Mauritius → UAE → Singapore → Maldives without repeating country facts. No arrows or quantitative scale.

beats.say: Date ढूँढ़ते समय issuance वाली rows चुनिए: Bhutan और Mauritius। Acceptance वाली row को issuance का प्रमाण मत बनाइए।
beats.on_screen: Highlight issuance rows, with 2020 and 2024 visible but not re-narrated. Issuance ≠ acceptance.

beats.say: इस visual को matching aid समझिए, worldwide coverage की पूरी list नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Read the specific note; do not infer universal acceptance.

beats.say: ₹1,000 की vaccination पक्की करनी हो, cash देना जरूरी है? सरकार आपके account में पैसे डालने के बजाय आपके लिए ₹1,000 voucher SMS या QR Code से भेजती है।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical vaccination: ₹1,000 voucher, not account credit.

beats.say: आप authorised centre पर उसी vaccination के लिए redeem करते हैं। पूरी redemption में unused value ₹1,000 से ₹0 होती है और vaccination 0 से 1।
beats.on_screen: Voucher → specified vaccination; ₹1,000 → ₹0 unused.

beats.say: ₹1,000 यहाँ समझाने के लिए लिया amount है, universal limit या किसी actual scheme का दावा नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Hypothetical illustration, not a universal voucher limit or reported scheme amount.

beats.say: यही 2021 का e-RUPI है: SMS/QR Code based Prepaid Cashless Electronic Voucher। National Payments Corporation of India, NPCI ने UPI platform पर बनाया; prepaid पहले funded, cashless यानी covered payment में cash नहीं देना।
beats.on_screen: e-RUPI • 2021 • NPCI • UPI platform; unpack prepaid and cashless.

beats.say: Person-specific यानी तय व्यक्ति; purpose-specific यानी तय काम। किसे देना है और किस काम पर इस्तेमाल होगा, अलग checks हैं; एक से दूसरा अपने-आप तय नहीं होता।
beats.on_screen: Two locks: person + purpose.

beats.say: Unrestricted account credit इसका non-example है; उसमें ये 2 locks नहीं हैं।
beats.on_screen: Boundary test: unrestricted account credit fails the voucher definition.

beats.say: Definition की पहचान रखिए: prepaid voucher, तय व्यक्ति और तय service।
beats.on_screen: Definition checkpoint: instrument + beneficiary + purpose.

beats.say: Phone पर app और coupon दोनों दिखें, तो समान हैं? Digital appearance समान है; e-RUPI restrictions वाला gift coupon जैसा है।
beats.on_screen: Common digital form, different functions.

beats.say: App interface है; e-RUPI voucher है, bank transfer या digital currency नहीं। Gift coupon की तुलना में भी intended beneficiary और intended service के locks रहेंगे।
beats.on_screen: Voucher versus app, transfer, currency; retain both locks.

beats.say: SMS delivery है, currency होने का प्रमाण नहीं; UPI platform भी इसे bank transfer नहीं बनाता।
beats.on_screen: Delivery medium ≠ instrument; underlying platform ≠ bank transfer.

beats.say: खास trap है e-RUPI बनाम Digital Rupee; gift coupon की analogy भी unrestricted या transferable money नहीं बनाती।
beats.on_screen: Confused pair: restricted voucher ≠ Digital Rupee; do not infer transferability.

beats.say: Comparison में appearance नहीं, काम और restrictions देखकर सही category चुनिए।
beats.on_screen: Difference table: app | bank transfer | currency | restricted voucher.

beats.say: ₹1,000 example का result क्या है? Vaccination मिलना, cash balance बढ़ना नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Process audit of the already-shown story: intended outcome = vaccination.

beats.say: इसमें government funding देती है, beneficiary इस्तेमाल करता है और authorised centre service देता है।
beats.on_screen: Freeze the existing story and label sponsor, user and redemption place; do not replay it.

beats.say: पहले SMS/QR voucher पहुँचता है, फिर redemption होता है; funded entitlement मिलता है, खुला account credit नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Annotate the existing flow: delivery precedes redemption; service entitlement rather than unrestricted credit.

beats.say: दूसरी खरीदारी allowed हो जाए, तो intended service तक मदद पहुँचने की guarantee टूट जाएगी।
beats.on_screen: Failure test: removing the purpose lock breaks targeted use.

beats.say: Fast run: सरकार भेजती है, beneficiary पाता है, centre पर service लेता है।
beats.on_screen: One brief animated run through the existing example.

beats.say: Delivery के बाद restricted redemption चाहिए; voucher मिलना service मिलना नहीं है।
beats.on_screen: Delivery → restricted redemption → intended outcome.

beats.say: सही service हो, लेकिन centre authorised न हो, तो चलेगा? नहीं; purpose के साथ place की condition भी है।
beats.on_screen: Apply a new boundary test: correct service but unauthorised centre → not permitted.

beats.say: ‘Only’ और ‘authorized’ allowed use बताते हैं; ‘not withdraw cash’ redemption को cash-out से अलग रखता है।
beats.on_screen: Evidence annotation on supplied wording: only for vaccination | authorized center | not withdraw cash or spend elsewhere.

beats.say: Allowed use पहचानते समय service और authorised place, दोनों जाँचिए।
beats.on_screen: Permission checklist: service AND place.

beats.say: किराना दुकान पर card से ₹1,000 दिए; seller को कितने मिलेंगे? Illustrated 2% fee में ₹20 कटेंगे, ₹980 पहुँचेंगे।
beats.on_screen: ₹1,000 sale − ₹20 fee = ₹980 receipt.

beats.say: यह Merchant Discount Rate, MDR है: seller की हर card transaction पर acquiring bank को दी जाने वाली fee। Acquirer दुकानदार की तरफ payment acceptance संभालता है।
beats.on_screen: MDR: merchant's acceptance fee to acquirer.

beats.say: Discount customer की price छूट नहीं है। Card acceptance की व्यवस्था की fee से merchant की net receipt कम होती है।
beats.on_screen: Not a price discount; acceptance service fee.

beats.say: Card sale और bank receipt का फर्क MDR समझाता है। अब इसके recipients देखिए।
beats.on_screen: Gross sale versus net receipt.

beats.say: Acquirer को fee दी तो पूरी उसी की? नहीं; payment में कई participants हैं, MDR उनके बीच share होती है।
beats.on_screen: One fee, multiple recipients.

beats.say: Acquiring Bank यानी दुकान को card से पैसे लेने की व्यवस्था देने वाला bank; Issuing Bank यानी आपको card देने वाला bank। Card Network और जहाँ लागू हो Payment Service Provider/Gateway भी fee share करते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Shop's card-acceptance arrangement → acquirer; your card → issuer; network and applicable provider also share MDR.

beats.say: Acquirer acceptance संभालता है, issuer card देता है, RuPay जैसे network messages जोड़ते हैं। Gateway/provider processing का interface दे सकता है, जैसे online checkout।
beats.on_screen: Participant roles; networks: RuPay, Visa, Mastercard.

beats.say: मिलकर payment चलाने वाले participants fee बाँटते हैं; collection point पूरी fee नहीं रखता। Individual percentages नहीं दिए हैं।
beats.on_screen: Collection ≠ sole retention; allocations unspecified.

beats.say: Acquirer, issuer, network और applicable provider याद रखें। Shared का मतलब equal shares नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Labelled participant recap without allocation percentages.

beats.say: MDR का direct payer कौन? Merchant, customer नहीं; खरीदारी का payment अलग है।
beats.on_screen: MDR payer: merchant.

beats.say: Customer ₹1,000 देता है, ₹1,020 नहीं। ₹20 merchant की तरफ कटते हैं; उसे ₹980 मिलते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Deduction on merchant side.

beats.say: Direct payer merchant है। Costs को prices में गिनना अलग economic सवाल है; उससे direct obligation नहीं बदलती।
beats.on_screen: Direct payer ≠ ultimate economic incidence.

beats.say: ये 3 boxes क्या जोड़ते हैं? Customer का gross payment, merchant की net receipt और participants की fee-sharing।
beats.on_screen: Customer → Merchant → Banks & Payment Network.

beats.say: बाएँ Customer से Merchant तक ₹1,000 arrow देखिए, जैसे पूरा bill चुकाना। यह gross purchase payment है, fee नहीं; percentage इसी base पर लगेगा।
beats.on_screen: Trace buyer → ₹1,000 → seller; gross base.

beats.say: बीच का Merchant seller है: payment अंदर, MDR shared arrow बाहर। जैसे मिली payment से खर्च अलग रखना, total ₹20 recipients की ओर जाते हैं; ₹980 बचते हैं।
beats.on_screen: Incoming gross; outgoing total fee; retained net.

beats.say: दाएँ grouped box कोई एक organisation नहीं: acquirer, issuer, RuPay/Visa/Mastercard जैसे networks और applicable provider समझिए। Individual shares नहीं दिखाए गए।
beats.on_screen: Expand grouped recipients; no equal-share assumption.

beats.say: 2% rate है: हर ₹100 पर ₹2। इसलिए ₹1,000 × 2 ÷ 100 से ₹20 fee मिलती है, ₹2 नहीं। ₹1,000 से ₹20 घटाइए: net receipt ₹980।
beats.on_screen: ₹1,000 × 2 ÷ 100 = ₹20 fee; ₹1,000 − ₹20 = ₹980 receipt. Distinguish rate from rupees.

beats.say: Figure में ₹1,000 gross = ₹980 net + ₹20 total fee। 2% illustrative है, universal rate नहीं।
beats.on_screen: Gross = net + total fee; illustrative rate.

beats.say: याद रखिए: RuPay network है, e-RUPI restricted voucher है, MDR merchant-paid fee है।
beats.on_screen: Network | restricted voucher | merchant fee.

notes.about: The unit connects RuPay card funding and overseas use, restricted e-RUPI redemption, and merchant-paid MDR. Its worked examples generally provide appropriate UPSC-level understanding.
key_questions: How do card funding, network identity, issuance and acceptance differ?
What makes e-RUPI person-specific and purpose-specific?
Who pays and shares MDR, and how does ₹1,000 become ₹980?
